title: Matrix bridge: kith Application Service for Matrix homeservers
description:
A Matrix Application Service (AS) bridge that makes kith chats accessible from any Matrix client, and transitively from Slack, Teams, Discord, IRC, and any other Matrix-bridged network.

Architecture:
- Implements the Matrix Application Service API (spec.matrix.org/v1.x/application-service-api)
- Runs alongside a Matrix homeserver (Synapse, Conduit, Dendrite) operated by the user
- Bridge registers as an AS with the homeserver via appservice registration YAML
- kith → Matrix: subscribe to kithd EventSource; on new message, PUT /rooms/{roomId}/send/{eventType}/{txnId} via homeserver Client-Server API using AS bot credentials
- Matrix → kith: receive transactions from homeserver at bridge's /_matrix/app/v1/transactions/{txnId}; call kithd Message/set create
- Each kith chat maps to a Matrix room; kith contacts map to virtual Matrix users (MSXIDs like @kith_alice:bridge.example.com)
- Room directory: bridge creates/joins rooms automatically on first message

Scope:
- AS registration file generation (homeserver-agnostic)
- Namespace claiming for user prefix (@kith_*) and room alias prefix (#kith_*)
- Message bridging: m.text ↔ kith body; m.file ↔ kith attachment
- Presence/read receipt bridging (Matrix m.read ↔ kith Peer/receipt)
- End-to-end: once kith↔Matrix works, Slack and Teams are reachable via existing Matrix bridges (matrix-appservice-slack, matrix-appservice-teams) with no additional kith code
- Target: Rust binary; ships with example Synapse/Conduit registration YAML and systemd unit

Why Matrix over direct Slack/Teams bridges:
- One implementation gives access to Slack, Teams, Discord, IRC, WhatsApp (via existing Matrix bridges)
- Matrix is federated and open; user controls the homeserver
- No per-network bot credentials to manage in kith itself
- Fits kith's no-central-server model: user runs homeserver + bridge on their own infra

Key decisions for research phase:
- Which homeserver to target first (Conduit is lighter; Synapse is most widely deployed)
- Whether to implement E2EE room bridging (complex; likely v2)
- Puppet users vs bot-only posting (puppeting gives correct sender identity in Matrix)
